questions.prompt: List the first twelve multiples of 4 and 5; identify the common multiples.
steps: Multiply 4 by each integer 1–12; repeat with 5.
Compare both lists and keep the values appearing in each. The LCM is 20; 60 is not in the first twelve multiples of 4.

questions.prompt: Evaluate (2/25) × 0.737 to one significant figure.
steps: The first significant digit is 5 and the next digit is 8; round it up to 6 in the hundredths place.

questions.prompt: Give the same product to three decimal places.
steps: The exact product is 0.05896.
Keep three digits after the decimal point, 058; the fourth digit is 9, so round 058 up to 059.

questions.prompt: Arrange 2/3, 4/7, 3/8 and 5/9 in ascending order.
steps: Order numerators: 189 < 280 < 288 < 336, then write the corresponding original fractions.

questions.prompt: Mericho’s population was 2,800 in 2016 and increased by 8% in 2017. Find the 2017 population.
steps: New population = 2800 + 224 = 3024.

questions.prompt: 1000 tonnes of maize are shared equally among 25 schools. How many kilograms does each receive?
steps: 1000 tonnes = 1,000,000 kg because 1 tonne = 1000 kg.
Divide 1,000,000 by 25 to obtain 40,000 kg.

questions.prompt: A radio cost Tsh 80,000 and was sold at 20% profit. Find profit and selling price.
steps: Profit percentage is calculated on cost: 0.20 × 80,000 = 16,000.
Selling price = cost + profit = 80,000 + 16,000 = 96,000.

questions.prompt: In trapezium ABCD, AD ∥ BC, A = 60°, D = 40°. At C, a is the upper exterior angle and c the interior angle; B = b. Find a,b,c.
steps: Co-interior angles on AB give b + 60 = 180, hence b = 120°.
Co-interior angles on CD give c + 40 = 180, hence c = 140°.
a and c form a straight angle, so a = 180 − 140 = 40° (also alternate interior to D).

questions.prompt: A square room has side 5 m. Find its perimeter and area.
steps: Perimeter = 4 × side = 4 × 5 = 20 m.
Area = side² = 5² = 25 m². Use squared units for area.

questions.prompt: If (6y + 1)/4 = 5(y + 5)/6, find y to three significant figures.
steps: Multiply by 12 to remove denominators: 3(6y + 1) = 10(y + 5).
Retain the first three significant digits 5,8,7; the following 5 rounds 7 up to 8.

questions.prompt: Solve 3x² − 7x − 6 = 0 by completing the square.
steps: Divide by 3: x² − (7/3)x = 2.
Take both square roots: x − 7/6 = ±11/6, so x = 18/6 = 3 or −4/6 = −2/3.

questions.prompt: Find the gradient through (−1,2) and (3,−5).
steps: Gradient = change in y divided by change in x.

questions.prompt: Find the image of P(−3,7) after reflection in the x-axis and y-axis.
questions.answer: In the x-axis: (−3,−7). In the y-axis: (3,7). If applied successively in both axes: (3,−7).
steps: Reflection in the x-axis maps (x,y) to (x,−y); reflection in the y-axis maps (x,y) to (−x,y).
Apply each to P for separate images. If both transformations are applied one after the other, both signs change.
questions.tip: The wording can mean separate reflections or successive reflections, so the distinction is shown explicitly.

questions.prompt: Solve 16^(3 − n) × 2^(1 + n) = 1/2; express n as an improper fraction.
steps: Rewrite 16 = 2⁴ and 1/2 = 2⁻¹.
Combine equal bases: 2^[4(3 − n) + (1 + n)] = 2⁻¹.
Equate exponents: 13 − 3n = −1, giving 3n = 14 and n = 14/3. Check 4(3 − 14/3) + 1 + 14/3 = −1.
questions.tip: The faint first exponent is 3 − n. The original wording and a clearer reproduction in the NECTA report confirm it.

questions.prompt: Solve log(2x² + 1) + log 4 = log(7x² + 8).
steps: Combine logarithms: log[4(2x² + 1)] = log(7x² + 8).
Equal logarithms of positive quantities have equal arguments: 8x² + 4 = 7x² + 8.
x² = 4, so x = ±2. Both arguments are positive for these values, so both are valid.

questions.prompt: DE ∥ BC, AD:BD = 3:5 and AC = 9.6 cm. Find AE.
steps: AB contains 3 + 5 = 8 ratio parts, so AD/AB = 3/8.
△ADE ∼ △ABC by AA; AE/AC = AD/AB = 3/8.
questions.tip: Use AD/AB = 3/8, not AD/BD = 3/5, when comparing the small triangle to the whole triangle.

questions.prompt: AB = AC and D is the midpoint of BC. Prove ∠ABD = ∠ACD.
steps: AB = AC is given; BD = DC because D is the midpoint; AD is shared.
Therefore △ABD ≅ △ACD by SSS. Corresponding angles at B and C are equal, establishing the required angle equality.

questions.prompt: A point is 80 m from a building and its angle of elevation is 25°. Find the height to one decimal place.
steps: Use the right triangle: height is opposite 25° and ground distance 80 m is adjacent.
To one decimal place, the height is 37.3 m.

questions.prompt: In right triangle ABC, AB = 6 m, AC = 8 m and the right angle is at A. Find BC.
steps: BC is the hypotenuse; apply Pythagoras: BC² = AB² + AC².
BC² = 6² + 8² = 100; take the positive square root to obtain 10 m.

questions.prompt: 250 students attended the first day, 350 the second, 150 both, and 10 neither. Without a Venn diagram find total enrolment.
steps: Add the daily totals, then remove the overlap counted twice: attended at least once = 250 + 350 − 150 = 450.
Include students absent on both days: total = 450 + 10 = 460.

questions.prompt: The pie-chart sectors are Kiswahili 210°, Mathematics 120°, Chemistry 30°. Find the fraction who passed Kiswahili.
steps: A complete pie chart represents 360°.

questions.prompt: Find the percentage who passed Mathematics.
steps: Mathematics fraction = 120/360 = 1/3.

questions.prompt: Find the percentage who passed Mathematics and Chemistry, as represented by their combined sectors.
steps: Add the sector angles: 120 + 30 = 150°.
questions.tip: The pie chart partitions students into separate categories. Here “and” asks for the combined categories; it does not provide data on individuals passing both subjects.
